html:
Utterly unengaging; reading it is like chewing wax. The descriptions of settings and of the characters’ inner lives are perfunctory in the extreme. The dialogue is bizarre, like lines from a soap opera, or from one of the comedy sketches on the Spring Festival Gala, China’s state TV New Year’s Eve show.

The characters’ values are warped: in under a hundred pages, misogyny crops up several times. I’m a man, and even I couldn’t stomach it. Were highly educated women in the 1990s really still unable to break free of five thousand years of “fine tradition”? In chapter 41, Xiao Yawen says: “Women—so much that’s cheap in us is born in our bones. As long as you’re a woman, you can never throw it off.” Did she time-travel here from the Qing dynasty?

After a hundred pages I still had no idea what kind of person the hero is. He reads like an idiot.

And its descriptions of Germany read exactly like the Germany fanboys on Zhihu, China’s answer to Quora.
